headline: Going Commando's USA v1.01 code matching rises from 85.49% to 87.68%
summary: The day's progress report puts USA v1.01 at 87.68% of code matched, up from 85.49%, with 7,950 of 8,580 functions matching. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. The largest merged batch, #399, converts 145 boot and level functions to C. A separate merged progress update reports 7,006 of 8,672 functions for PAL and 7,612 of 8,634 for USA v2.00.
highlights: #396 matches two Oozla routines, #397 corrects an entry before matching a boot function, and #398 adds nine routines including route following and trail creation.
#401 repairs catalogue entries and matches 13 routines. #405 adds four initialization functions, while #407 matches logarithms and HUD range, visibility and colour handling.
#393 adds functional C for the native port, and #402 restores 27 tested helper rows. These reconstructions and #404's effect repairs are separate from exact code matching.
#406 classifies 37 routines as original assembly rather than new C. It leaves the progress reports unchanged.
The Joba NPC state machine (#408), a hit-packet routine (#409) and Tabora's hero-trigger reset (#411) are open proposals. Their claimed matches have not landed.
#412 proposes returning three more functional rows and remains unmerged. #410 corrects the port handoff: Feltzin's difference came from the interpreter's sound mask, and Gorn's from frame load.
